HISTORY AND PHYSICAL (H&P)

History:
• 41-year-old male (DOB 16-May-1982) awoke at 05:30 with a sudden, severe, left-sided headache.  
• Headache persistent at time of call; more intense than his usual frontally distributed headaches.  
• Mild photophobia; transient early-morning dizziness now resolved.  
• No neck stiffness, no fever, no significant nausea or vomiting.  
• Pain slightly improves after settling in bed but remains present; paracetamol provided no relief.  
• No prior migraines; no family history of migraine.  
• Reports ↑ work stress for ~2 months with late nights and variable mood but denies current severe anxiety or depression and denies suicidal ideation.

Past Medical History:
• Generalised anxiety disorder (≈2 years).  
• No hypertension or other chronic illnesses reported.  
• Family history: mother with anxiety; no notable physical illnesses.

Medications:
• Sertraline – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Paracetamol (self-administered today) – dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Physical Examination: (teleconsultation – limited)
• Patient alert, coherent, answering questions appropriately.  
• Reports unilateral (left) headache.  
• No neck stiffness.  
• Afebrile by history.  
• Mild light sensitivity; no current nausea.  
• No focal neurological deficits reported.

Impression:
• Unilateral headache – probable migraine vs tension-type headache.

Management Plan:
• Start Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented) as first-line migraine analgesia; may continue paracetamol if needed.  
• Advise hydration 1.5–2 L non-caffeinated fluids daily.  
• Encourage 7–8 hours sleep nightly.  
• Consider taking up to 1 week off work (self-certify) to reduce stress.  
• Provide self-referral link to local counselling service for stress management.  
• Supply written information on headache red-flag symptoms; advise low threshold for re-contacting GP or urgent care if red flags occur.  
• Schedule follow-up appointment in 1 week; if no improvement, consider blood tests and further evaluation.

Patient Summary:
Mr. Ayrton Warren developed a new, severe left-sided headache this morning with mild photophobia and poor response to paracetamol. Clinical picture most consistent with migraine or tension headache, likely stress-related. He will trial ibuprofen, address hydration, sleep and occupational stress, and follow up in one week.

Key Takeaways:
• Begin ibuprofen for acute pain; continue paracetamol if required.  
• Maintain good hydration and adequate nightly sleep.  
• Seek medical review sooner if headache worsens, new neurological symptoms, fever, or other red-flag signs develop.

Next Steps:
• One-week GP follow-up (telephone or in person).  
• If persistent/worsening symptoms → blood tests and further assessment.  
• Patient to self-refer for counselling; consider work leave to reduce stress.
